contentBlocks.body: Throwing new Error("something failed") tells a caller that something went wrong but not what kind of problem it was. Callers end up matching on message strings, which break as soon as someone rewords a message. A custom error class gives each failure a type you can check with instanceof, plus structured fields such as the field name that failed validation.

When you catch a low-level error and throw a more meaningful one, do not throw away the original. The cause option (ES2022) keeps it attached, so logs show the whole chain: what the program was trying to do and what actually broke underneath.

Exceptions are best for unexpected failures. For outcomes a caller must handle, such as validation of user input, many codebases return a result object instead: { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error }. The caller cannot forget the failure case, because it has to check ok before it can reach the value, and batch processing can keep going past one bad row.
catch (error) {} with an empty body swallows every error, including your own bugs. Catch narrowly: check the type, handle what you expect, and rethrow the rest.
Set this.name in custom errors. Without it the error prints as a generic Error, and loggers that group by name cannot tell your failures apart.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why check error instanceof ValidationError instead of matching error.message?

choices: the type survives message rewording and can carry extra fields
instanceof is faster than string comparison
messages are not available in catch blocks
payload.answer: the type survives message rewording and can carry extra fields
payload.explanation: Messages are for humans and change; types and fields are a contract for code.

knowledgeItems.prompt: What does new Error("save failed", { cause: err }) add compared with new Error("save failed")?

choices: a longer message that includes err.message
an error.cause property pointing at the original error
payload.answer: an error.cause property pointing at the original error
payload.explanation: cause keeps the underlying error attached so the full chain can be logged.

knowledgeItems.prompt: In the lesson's tryParseAge, what happens when parseAge throws a TypeError?

choices: it becomes { ok: true, value: undefined }
payload.explanation: Only expected ValidationErrors become results; anything else is a bug and keeps propagating.

payload.text: In a custom error constructor, setting this.____ = "ValidationError" makes logs and stack traces show the right type.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Import rows with a ValidationError class and result objects, so one bad row no longer aborts the whole batch.
